entries.clue: Fighter with height and strength (5)

blocks.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
HT is the standard abbreviation for height

annotation.surface: A boxer blessed with reach and power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' looks like a boxer; it is the aircraft, and 'with' simply puts the height after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: power and force, as in 'with all his might'.

entries.clue: Daily consuming a drink beginning to rant, confusing speaker (3,8)

indicatorNotes.consuming: to consume is to take in and swallow, so the cleaner's name swallows the other letters

kept as it is
to lap is to drink, as a cat does
first letter of rant

annotation.surface: A cleaning lady has a drink and starts ranting incoherently.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is British for a cleaner who comes in by the day. The character comes from Sheridan's play The Rivals.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by character: Sheridan's Mrs Malaprop confuses words that sound alike, giving us 'malapropism'.

entries.clue: Count on time for hard work (5)

blocks.note: Graf is the German title for a count
T is the abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: A reminder that you can rely on time to deliver the results of hard work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Count on' reads as the phrase 'rely on'; 'Count' is the German nobleman.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal use: to graft is to toil, and the noun means sustained labour.

entries.clue: Identical schemes formulated for so-called economics (3,6,7)

indicatorNotes.formulated: to formulate is to put together into a new form, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 16 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An economist complaining that every policy offered is the same.
annotation.walkthrough: 'So-called' is there because the answer is a nickname, coined by Thomas Carlyle.
annotation.definitionFit: A nickname: Carlyle's gloomy label for economics, after Malthus's forecasts.

entries.clue: Sauce is excellent (7)

blocks.note: something poured over the top of a dish
dated upper-class British slang for first-rate

annotation.surface: A diner's verdict: the sauce is superb.
annotation.walkthrough: The praise word is old-fashioned British slang, like 'ripping' or 'spiffing'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: what goes on top of food, such as a sauce, and a dated word for first-rate.

entries.clue: Exchange some jazz with a German (5-2)

blocks.note: trad is traditional jazz, one kind of jazz
ein is German for 'a'

annotation.surface: A jam session swapping numbers with a German musician.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A German' is the word 'a' in German, not a German person.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: handing over an old car or phone as part payment for a new one is an exchange.

entries.clue: Feeble, one makes way for Leonard, becoming generous (9)

blocks.note: pitiful = feeble, pathetic
one = I, the letter that leaves (the first I)
Len is short for Leonard

annotation.surface: A weak man steps aside for Leonard, who turns out to be kind-hearted.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the first I of the feeble word goes; the second stays.
annotation.definitionFit: Generous in the sense of ample: a generous helping is an abundant one.

entries.clue: In panic holding gun over person who’s on your case (12)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold something is to keep it in your grip, so IN TERROR keeps the gun inside

blocks.note: in terror = in panic
gat is old American slang for a gun
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

annotation.surface: Someone panics while holding a gun on a detective.
annotation.walkthrough: The gun and the over go in together, just before the final R.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone 'on your case' is questioning and pressing you, which is a questioner's job.

entries.clue: Put up flag over jetty and decking (10)

indicatorNotes.Put up: in a down entry, putting up turns the word upward, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.over: in a down entry, GAR sits over LANDING

blocks.note: a rag is a scrappy flag; it goes up, giving GAR
a landing stage or jetty

annotation.surface: Instructions for raising a flag above a jetty with a timber deck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decking' reads as timber boarding beside the jetty; here it means decorating.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to deck is to adorn, and hanging wreaths of flowers is one way to do it.

entries.clue: Prepared to fight a crowd, one shown the way around island (9)

indicatorNotes.around: around means on every side of, so the letters for 'shown the way' surround IS

blocks.note: a mob is a crowd
one = I
led = shown the way
IS is the abbreviation for island

annotation.surface: A man ready to take on a crowd after being guided round an island.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one man's story, but 'Prepared to fight' is the definition and everything after it is wordplay.

entries.clue: Have a meal, in my case non-vegetarian (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the meal goes inside

blocks.note: kept as it is, the case
to eat is to have a meal

annotation.walkthrough: 'In my case' looks like 'as for me'; read literally it is an instruction about a container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense: food full of meat is the opposite of vegetarian.

entries.clue: Stay a long time securing lease for best floor of building (3,5)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure is to hold fast, so BE AGE holds the lease tight inside

blocks.note: to be is to stay or remain, as in 'let it be'
an age = a long time
a let is a lease on a property

annotation.surface: A tenant staying for years who has signed a lease on a building's finest storey.
annotation.walkthrough: The term is French, 'fine floor': the grand first floor of a European town house, holding the main reception rooms.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French term for the principal storey of a grand house.

entries.clue: Dawdle around centre of hotel in Germany (6)

blocks.note: the last letter of hotel, all of 'in' and the first three of Germany

annotation.walkthrough: 'Centre of hotel' wants to be the letter T; instead it points into the middle of the whole phrase 'hotel in Germany'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to stay on and be slow to leave.

entries.clue: Bombardment, singular punishment for sinners (9)

blocks.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
the fire of hell that awaits sinners

annotation.surface: A preacher describing the unique torment awaiting the wicked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singular' reads as 'remarkable' in the surface; it is just the grammar abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense: artillery shells fired at a target make up a bombardment.

entries.clue: Does gossip about second one Holmes may be seen with (11)

annotation.definition: one Holmes may be seen with

blocks.note: does are female deer
S is the abbreviation for second
a gossip is a talker

annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like the verb; it is the plural of doe. 'One' in the definition is a thing, not a person.

entries.clue: Some woman accepting a reduced prize, free programs (9)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so the woman takes the other letters inside

blocks.note: she = some woman
kept as it is
REWARD without its D

annotation.walkthrough: 'Some woman' is the pronoun, the usual crossword way to ask for a generic woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A computing term: software handed out free, usually to try before paying.

entries.clue: Ignore wind at centre of storm catching an awning (4,1,5,3)

indicatorNotes.catching: to catch is to grab and hold, so the storm's centre holds the awning, which ends up straight after TURN

blocks.note: a road winds, or turns
a blind is an awning or shade
the eye of a storm is its centre

annotation.surface: Advice to pay no attention to the wind in a storm's heart snagging a canopy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the weather beside 'storm', but it is the verb that rhymes with 'find', meaning twist.

entries.clue: A way to travel: on the pillion? (7)

blocks.note: kept as it is
ST is short for street, a way
to ride is to travel

annotation.surface: A suggested means of getting about: riding pillion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A way to travel' pretends to be one phrase meaning a mode of transport, and it splits into three. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a pillion passenger sits with one leg each side of the motorbike.

entries.clue: Understand your old walls to be weak (7)

indicatorNotes.walls: to wall something is to enclose it, so THY forms walls round the reading

blocks.note: thy is the old word for your
to read a situation is to understand it

annotation.walkthrough: 'Walls' looks like a noun in the surface; it is the verb.

entries.clue: Greatly enlarges barrel wood suppliers stock (7)

indicatorNotes.stock: to stock something is to keep it in store, so the trees hold the barrel inside

blocks.note: trees supply wood
BL is an abbreviation for barrel

annotation.surface: Timber merchants massively increasing their stock of barrels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like a noun about merchandise; it is the verb, meaning hold.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: multiplying by three is a great enlargement.

entries.clue: A denial of evolution deliberately started quarrel (8,4,6)

blocks.note: an argument is a quarrel
something started on purpose began from design

annotation.surface: A creationist deliberately picking a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a philosophical term: the claim that nature's complexity proves a designer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the teleological case for a creator, set against evolution by natural selection.

entries.clue: Feel uncertainly around unlit yard at first, then steadier (3-4)

indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the fumbling word goes round the two letters

blocks.note: to grope is to feel your way uncertainly
first letters of unlit and yard

annotation.surface: Someone fumbling around a dark yard before finding their feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steadier' looks like a comparative adjective; it is a noun, something that steadies. Campers trip over these in the dark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the line pegged to the ground keeps a tent or mast steady.

entries.clue: Greetings unfortunately upset a young lady (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down entry, ALAS is turned upside down, reading upward

blocks.note: alas = unfortunately
kept as it is
Ms, the title for a woman

annotation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately upset' reads as an anagram signal; it is ALAS, then turned upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: the Arabic greeting 'peace', and the low bow that goes with it.

entries.clue: Still a desire for unsuitable food (4)

blocks.note: a still is a photograph, or pic
kept as it is

annotation.surface: Someone still craving bad food.

annotation.surface: A reference to Orwell's memoir Down and Out in Paris and London.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue names Orwell's book, but the answer is a different book set in the same two cities, full of the downtrodden. 'Down' also marks that it is a down entry.

entries.clue: Coupé, not safe, breaks down but it is found appealing (4,3,2,3)
